newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - June 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - June 12.

text.p: In the fight for the hearts of consumers, Woolworths Ltd and Coles Myer Ltd will embark on packaging "meal solutions", a new market segment which falls between fast food and traditional cooking and is the fastest growing sector in the A$21 billion a year fresh food market. Page 1.

Australian Bureau of Statistics figures released yesterday show home lending rose 12.2 per cent in seasonally adjusted terms in April to a three-year high, but despite this, a National Australia Bank survey showed both corporate Australia and consumers stll have lingering doubts about the strength of the economy. Page 3.

Production figures released yesterday by the Australian Winemakers Federation for the recently completed 1997 vintage show the wine industry has posted a record premium grape harvest of 500,000 tonnes, and indicates the rising popularity of chardonnay and shiraz in Australia. Page 3.

The new United States ambassador to Australia, Genta Hawkins Holmes, said yesterday her country understands Australia's concerns about international climate-change talks, and would work with Australia to reach a compromise. Holmes comments show a softening in the attitude of the United States towards Australia's isolated stance on the issue. Page 5.

Federal Industry Minister John Moore yesterday acknowledged the Federal Government needed to address insecurity over economic reform in the community, and said this insecurity was contributing to a flat domestic economy as the public is reluctant to spend. Moore also indicated the Government would not follow through on Productivity Commission recommendations to cut tariffs in the textile, clothing and footwear industries. Page 1.

While releasing a study on Japan that urges Australian companies to stop considering Japan a closed and difficult market, Foreign Affairs Minister Alexander Downer said yesterday racist sentiments could affect thousands of jobs resulting from Asian trade nd investment. Page 1.

Aussie Home Loans has been forced to change the wording of its commercials after an action by competitor FAI Home Loans in the Federal Court. The Aussie Home Loans commercial had stated it had the lowest standard variable mortgage rate of any major lender - the company will now advertise that no major bank has a lower rate than it does. Page 1.

Recent figures show the three largest private insurers in Australia suffered a 117 per cent lift in claims for delinquent homes in 1996, an indication that borrowers are increasingly defaulting on their home loans amid an atmosphere of aggressive lending ractices. Page 1.

The search for kidnap victim Kerry Whelan has shifted to one of the several hundred disused mine shafts in the rugged Morton National Park near Goulburn, with 30 police officers scouring a large tract of land in the area. The area being searched is at the rear of a Bungonia property owned by Bruce Burrell, a former employee of Mrs Whelan's husband Bernard. Page 1.

Carol Burrowes, the supervising co-ordinator of the Holyoake program, a service at Neutral Bay for families affected by drug or alcohol problems, says some parents whose children are on drugs resort to taking pills found in their child's bedrooms to a chemist for analysis. Page 1.

New South Wales Legal Services Commissioner Steve Mark has published 10 case studies of complaints about individual legal practitioners, such as that of a Sydney lawyer who charged his client for 27 hours in one day, and hopes the publication will cause errant barristers and solicitors in the State to understand why there are so many complaints. Page 3.

In an attempt to halt the influx of heroin and designer drugs coming on to the streets of Melbourne from Sydney, Victorian police are considering setting up road blocks between Victoria and New South Wales. The radical plans would see people in any mode of transport being checked for illicit drugs. Page 1.

A medical research paper shows the Victorian Children's Welfare Department authorised the use of young children from a State orphanage in a post-war experiment involving trials of a whooping cough vaccine by the Commonwealth Serum Laboratories. Page 1.

Federal Cabinet this week approved a compromise plan that will see Essendon Airport remain open, but in the hands of private operators. The Federal Government will sell the airport, and satisfy rural demands to keep it open, while at the same time ending Commonwealth subsidies. Page 1.

Victorian Liberal MP Bruce Atkinson is under further pressure following confirmation last night he worked on a State Government-funded project while a member of Parliament, a move that is a violation of the State Constitution. The Labor Opposition revealed material showing Atkinson was a retail "sub-consultant" on the Urban Villages Project for East Richmond in March 1995. Page 1.
